newsitem.title: USA: Santa Fe says still weighing Newmont bid.
newsitem.headline: Santa Fe says still weighing Newmont bid.

text.p: Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp said Tuesday it met executives from Newmont Mining Corp but did not yet decide on Newmont's hostile bid for Santa Fe Pacific.
Santa Fe Pacific chief executive Patrick James said the company was also "continuing to work" with Homestake Mining Co on its friendly merger proposal with Santa Fe.
"We've not yet made a determination regarding the Newmont proposal," James said in a conference call following Santa Fe Pacific's fourth quarter results.
James said there was "no specific timetable" on the talks with Newmont. "We've had meetings and we're going to continue to have meetings" with Newmont, he said.
Newmont is offering 0.4 Newmont shares for each Santa Fe share, after Santa Fe rejected an earlier offer of 0.33 share.
The friendly merger with Homestake would give Santa Fe shareholders 1.115 Homestake shares for each Santa Fe share.
In morning trading, Santa Fe was flat at 15-3/4, with Newmont unchanged at 40-5/8 and Homestake up 1/8 at 14-1/4.
In weighing both proposals, Santa Fe's board will "look very hard at the near- and intermediate- and long-term value and potential value of the transactions," James said.
"We're going to try to get the very best value for shareholders," he added.
